newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 23.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading.

* Recent sell-off may ease after the Dow's overnight gain, the second largest in its history, but market will remain weak and tentative due to lingering concerns about the beleagured property sector, says Abacus Securities Corp research director Erwin Tan.
* All-Asia Securities research head Helen Alvarez said support is seen at 2,800 points and once broken, the market may be headed for more carnage.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index ended lower by 84.53 points to 2,860.45.
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones rose 173.38 points to 6,833.59. PLDT's ADR was unchanged at $57 5/8.
* Empire East Land Holdings Inc, mass housing unit of Megaworld Properties & Holdings, denied runours in the stock market that it was about to declare bankruptcy.
* Philippine president Fidel Ramos stepped in to say the local property sector was not about to crash in reaction to fears by market analysts.
* A senior Philippine Central Bank official told Reuters that outstanding bank loans of Megaworld and Empire East were in order.
* Purefoods Corp said it posted a net income of 19.3 million pesos for the first quarter of the year from a net loss of 108 million pesos.
* Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co has mandated Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to arrange a $140 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
* The coupon on the Philippines' maiden 20-year treasury bond was set at 14.375 percent at an oversubscribed auction on Tuesday.

* Newspaper Manila Bulletin quoted Finance Minister Roberto de Ocampo as saying that the passage of the last component of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Program by May 1 may be unlikely due to time constraint.

* Times Journal said cellular phone company Pilipino Telephone Corp (Piltel) signed a cross-ownership agreement with Philippine Global Communications Inc (Philcom) where Piltel sells five billion pesos worth of its shares to Philcom at 20 per share. Piltel will also have the option to acquire 20 percent interest in Philcom.
* Manila Chronicle said at least three food conglomerates are expected to participate in the auction of cash-strapped Victorias Milling Co within the next 15 to 30 days.

* The Philippine Star said the country's gross international reserves level reached $12.389 billion as of March 20 up $644 million from the $11.745 billion level end of 1996, Central Bank data showed.
* The peso closed lower at 26.368 vs the dollar at 26.361.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.03125 percent.
